analysis: Uniform per-user transition weighting achieved macro validation HR@10 0.520, improving on the supplied prior result of 0.495 and baseline reference of 0.505. Category HR@10: Movies_and_TV 0.535, Industrial_and_Scientific 0.530, Electronics 0.400, CDs_and_Vinyl 0.615. Electronics recovered from 0.345 but remained below its 0.420 baseline reference. This supports uniform supervision over the previous exponential recency weighting in this run; it does not establish the cause or statistical significance. The host reported success with 479.05 allocated GPU-seconds. No test results were available.
code_summary: One independently trained SASRec model and one selected checkpoint per category, with dataset routing and no ensemble. Each network uses 96-dimensional embeddings, two causal attention blocks with two heads, and a jointly trained gated cumulative-taste feature. Scoring uses normalized embeddings, a learned scale, and item biases. Training retains sampled cross-entropy with 192 shared uniform negatives, complete training-history/current-positive exclusion, random windows, AdamW, seed 42, and the environment-controlled 200-epoch default. The sole change replaces exponential recency weights with uniform valid-transition weights normalized per user. Predictor loading, validation checkpoint selection, supplied splits, and trial-local artifacts remain unchanged.
